extraction.Name: Blanche Goings
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her 640 acre allotment, for she did not want to pay taxes on it; but the Indian Agency informed her that it would be reported to the tax collector, that she would have the taxes to pay, so she accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: she got behind in taxes, and, about 1921, she borrowed money—$245.00— of John Nelson, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, paying the taxes with this money; that she repaid this loan, clearing the land; that later she sold the land to a Mr. Potts, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $7500.00, cash
extraction.Buyer: Mr. Potts, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $7500.00, cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she got behind in taxes, and, about 1921, she borrowed money—$245.00— of John Nelson, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, paying the taxes with this money; she considers that this was a poor price for her land, and if it had not been for receiving the patent in fee, with the consequent taxes, she would not have sold her allotment
extraction.Occupation/Income: her only source of income is by doing house work and common labor for other people
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; health generally not good; has three children to support; health of her children is good; has never received any help from the County, State or the United States Government; allotment was 640 acres; document dated November 1928
